audit.whatIsWrong: Five of seven rows disagreed with their own whys text: level 3 was Quinn against 'you contest evenly', levels 4-5 were Skill against 'Quinn's ranged harass still keeps you off her', level 6 was Quinn against 'Level 6 is even', first item was Skill against 'Quinn kites your first-item all-ins and stays ahead', and 2+ items was Quinn against 'your DPS and R re-engage overwhelm her escape'.
audit.why: The packet chart (Quinn / Quinn / Skill / Quinn / Skill / Quinn / Yone) matches the prose row for row, and the mirror (quinn__yone) already fixed rows 4 and 6 to Skill and Yone respectively — so packet and mirror agree.
audit.corrected: Rows 3-7 aligned as matched full/content pairs with ratings and rewritten phases[].why lines.

audit.whatIsWrong: Vault and Blinding Assault drove every piece of advice on the page without a cooldown attached, so 'commit on Vault's cooldown' had no number.
audit.why: Vault is 12/11/10/9/8s and Blinding Assault 11/10.5/10/9.5/9s — close enough together that she can chain them, which is exactly why the early rows are hers, and far enough apart late to give a window.
audit.corrected: Both numbers written into dosFull[0].d, report[5].t, spikes[0].text, early, phases[2].why and phases[3].why.

audit.whatIsWrong: Four fields said Blinding Assault blinds Yone and makes his autos miss ('blinds your autos to zero', 'your AAs miss under the blind'). Riot's description says the ability marks an enemy and HINDERS ITS VISION — it obscures sight, it does not cause attacks to miss. Vault's brief interrupt on arrival and the fact that it lands her back near maximum attack range were never mentioned anywhere. Fate Sealed was again called a knockup setter; it is a blink behind the last champion in a line plus a pull.
audit.why: Riot ability text in the brief, which is the authority here; the mirror recorded the same Fate Sealed correction. A Yone told his autos are blinded plays the trade completely differently from one told he has lost vision of her.
audit.corrected: Blind replaced with vision-hinder everywhere it appeared, Vault restated as dash-in / brief interrupt / land at max range, and Fate Sealed restated as blink-behind-and-pull.

audit.why: Unlike other pages in this champion's set, report[8].t here does not call for anti-heal, which is right — there is no meaningful healing in this matchup.

edits.before: Full kit online — your core pattern starts now. Keep the wave near your side so Quinn must walk into your engage range.
edits.after: Full kit online and it evens out — her Q is 10s at rank 1, so the gap between pokes is where your pattern lives.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Vault's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: Hers again: Blinding Assault plus Vault out-harass you at 4-5. Give up CS rather than health and wait on Blade of the Ruined King.

edits.before: Fate Sealed sets up team knockups nothing can dodge. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Quinn's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Fate Sealed blinks behind her and pulls, it is not a knockup — but Vault answers it, so spend R only once her E is down.

edits.before: Blade of the Ruined King is your spike — force fights the moment it completes, on Vault's cooldown.
edits.after: Blade of the Ruined King helps, but with Vault up she kites the all-in — force only once her E is spent.

edits.before: Fate Sealed sets up team knockups nothing can dodge — build your teamfight around that. Quinn carry threat: 8.5/10 — shift to picks and wave control if he gets ahead.
edits.after: Fate Sealed blinks behind their back line and pulls it to you — build your teamfight around that. Quinn carry threat: 8.5/10 — shift to picks and wave control if she gets ahead.

edits.before: Her self-peel. Q3-R when it’s down. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: Vault is 8-12s: it dashes in, interrupts, then drops her at max range.

edits.before: Quinn wastes Vault (Dash/Blind) — commit the full pattern immediately.
edits.after: Vault's brief interrupt can cut a cast — respect it mid-commit.

edits.before: That is Quinn's favourite window — refuse it and half his win condition is gone.
edits.after: Blinding Assault hinders your vision — you lose sight of her while she kites away.

edits.before: Track Quinn's Vault (Dash/Blind): Her self-peel. Q3-R when it’s down. When it is down — Q3-R her.
edits.after: Vault dashes in, briefly interrupts you, and leaves her at max attack range. 8-12s — commit inside it.

edits.before: Quinn's Blinding Assault blinds your autos and out-ranges you at level 1.
edits.after: Blinding Assault hinders your vision and out-ranges you at level 1.

edits.before: Quinn's Blinding Assault (Q) plus Vault (E) reset is a huge chunk on any melee that walks up; if she lands Q she out-trades you cleanly since your AAs miss under the blind.
edits.after: Blinding Assault (Q) on 9-11s plus Vault (E) on 8-12s chunks any melee that walks up; the Q hinders your vision, so you lose sight of her while she kites the trade out.

edits.before: Quinn owns the first levels: Blinding Assault (Q) blinds your autos to zero while its slow lets her stack a full ranged combo, and her Vault (E) both disengages and refreshes trade windows. Respect her range, dodge Q, and just farm with Mortal Steel (Q) pokes rather than committing.
edits.after: Quinn owns the first levels: Blinding Assault (Q) hinders your vision on a 9-11s cooldown, and Vault (E) dashes to you, briefly interrupts, then leaves her back at max attack range — disengage and re-poke in one button. Respect her range, dodge Q, and farm with Mortal Steel pokes.

notes: Riot's text for Blinding Assault says it marks an enemy and hinders its vision — the page called it a blind that makes your autos miss, in four places. Vault's brief interrupt on arrival was missing entirely and is the reason a raw commit into her fizzles.
